input.command: find src -type f; cat package.json; grep -rn "runnable\|createFixTask\|poll" src
input.description: List source files and search usages
Show store.ts and search for task usages

input.reason: In src/tasks.ts, createFixTask builds `task` with `feedback: null` (line 14) and inserts it (line 15). It writes the feedback to the store in a separate `store.update` (line 16) but never changes the local `task` object. Line 17 then emits `{ ...task }`, and line 18 returns `task`, so both always carry `feedback: null`. The claim that `poll` can pick up the task between the two writes is not supported. `poll` only runs what `store.runnable()` returns, and the only TaskStore in the repository is the interface in src/tasks.ts. src/store.ts has repo methods and no task store. Nothing in the working tree shows `runnable()` returning a task that is already in the `running` state, so I removed the poll clause and kept the emit claim.

findings.text: `createFixTask` inserts the task as `running` with `feedback: null` and writes the feedback in a second statement. `emit` sends `{ ...task }` with the stale `null` feedback.
findings.reason: These claims hold: the task is inserted as `running` with `feedback: null` (lines 14-15), the feedback goes in a second `store.update` (line 16), and `emit({ ...task })` (line 17) sends the local object. That object is never updated, so its feedback is still null. The claim that `poll` can pick up the task between the two writes and run it without feedback is not supported. `poll` runs only what `store.runnable()` returns. `TaskStore` is just an interface here, and no implementation exists in the working tree (src/store.ts handles repos only). So nothing shows that `runnable()` returns a task already marked `running`. I deleted that clause.

evidence.code: const task: Task = { id, state: "running", feedback: null };

input.severity_reason: This happens on every createFixTask call, not just in a race. `store.update` never changes the local object, so the emitted event and the returned task always have `feedback: null`. That is wrong behavior on the main path. It is not Critical because the stored record still gets the feedback, so no data is lost or corrupted.
